correctness.rationale: For star with n leaves plus k disjoint leaf-leaf edges, two independent CONTINUOUS-TIME walkers jump at unit total rate, initially uniform among distinct peripheral unordered pairs. The six symmetry classes HU,HP,UU,UP,PPsame,PPdiff yield the displayed exact rational M_{n,k}, with boundary states k=0 and n=2k solved separately. Subtracting neighboring k yields positive rational difference whose numerator is a polynomial in k>=0 and u=n-2(k+1)>=0 with all coefficients positive except -1235, dominated by 5264k+1404u under n>=3. Exactly k adjacent initial peripheral pairs give first-order collision probability 2k/[n(n-1)]t, versus O(t²) for the star. The maximum-matching / original-star mean ratio tends to 5/2. Independent exact rational Poisson solution of the full unordered pair chain confirmed n=3..8 cases.

value.rationale: PASS. The result is a sharp nontrivial graph perturbation counterexample to naive 'adding edges speeds walker meetings' for a natural nested family: initial collision probability rises linearly, yet mean first-collision time strictly increases with each disjoint added edge. The persistent asymptotic slowdown factor 5/2 makes it more than an isolated small-graph computation.
